summary: Syria's ruling Ba'ath party nominates Bashar al-Assad for president and the constitution is changed to allow him to succeed his father, Hafez al-Assad, who died on 2000-06-10.

Rifaat al-Assad, the exiled uncle of Bashar al-Assad, challenges Bashar's succession to power in Syria, while the Syrian military reportedly rallies around Bashar and orders are issued to arrest Rifaat if he tries to attend his brother's funeral.
Bashar al-Assad, designated heir, appeared at his father Hafez al-Assad's funeral in Damascus, flanked by Syria's defence minister, as world leaders paid tribute.
Bashar al-Assad was elected general secretary of the ruling Ba'ath party, consolidating his hold on power.

Bashar al-Assad gave an inaugural speech promising constructive criticism, transparency, and democracy, but within a year his government began cracking down on dissidents, journalists, and human rights critics.
Syria's new president Bashar al-Assad orders the release of 600 political prisoners to mark the 30th anniversary of the purge that brought his father Hafez to power.

Reporters Sans Frontieres places Syrian President Bashar al-Assad on its list of "predators of press freedom" after Syria refused to renew the credentials of the only resident foreign correspondent in the country.
Asma Assad accompanies her husband, Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, to Britain for Syria's first official visit, during which she is to be presented to the Queen at Buckingham Palace.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad held talks with Tony Blair in Downing Street, with both leaders acknowledging differences over Iraq but describing the talks as realistic and constructive.
Tens of thousands of Syrians rallied in Damascus in a government-organized demonstration supporting President Bashar al-Assad amid international pressure to withdraw troops from Lebanon.
Bashar al-Assad meets UN envoy Terje Roed-Larsen in Damascus as the UN demands full Syrian withdrawal from Lebanon.
President Bashar al-Assad's ruling Ba'ath party conference in Damascus is heralded by Assad as a "great leap" towards reform, amid reports that Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam is to step down.

UN special envoy Terje Roed-Larsen is flying to Damascus this weekend for urgent talks with Syrian President Bashar al-Assad amid concern that Syrian intelligence agents are still operating in Lebanon.

Syria's ruling Ba'ath party, headed by President Bashar al-Assad, expels former vice-president Abdel-Halim Khaddam and intends to try him for treason after he alleged that Assad personally threatened Rafik Hariri before Hariri's assassination.

The UN commission investigating the assassination of former Lebanese prime minister Rafik Hariri requests to interview Syria's president Bashar al-Assad, after Syria's former vice-president Abdul Halim Khaddam said in a television interview that Assad had threatened Hariri a few months before his murder.

Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad arrives in Damascus for a two-day visit to Syria, where he is scheduled to hold talks with Syrian counterpart Bashar al-Assad on bilateral agreements and relations with the wider world.
US President George Bush pledged money to Lebanon but offered only rhetoric toward Damascus and Tehran, as Syrian President Bashar al-Assad remained unwilling to talk to the Bush administration.
Bashar al-Assad is the only candidate in Syria's presidential referendum, with celebrations held before any ballots were cast.
The US sends a new ambassador and top diplomat to Damascus, marking a renewed engagement with Bashar al-Assad after years of isolation.
Human Rights Watch reports that Syria's human rights record has failed to improve in the 10 years since President Bashar al-Assad came to power.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad is expected to visit Beirut for the first time since the 2005 assassination of former Lebanese prime minister Rafiq al-Hariri, for a joint visit with King Abdullah of Saudi Arabia to attend an Arab mini-summit.
Syrian security forces reportedly killed four people in an attack on the Omari mosque in Deraa during protests, marking the most serious unrest in President Bashar al-Assad's 11-year rule.

Syrian government forces reportedly opened fire on protesters in Daraa, killing at least nine people, amid calls for reform and pledges by an adviser to President Bashar al-Assad to consider protesters' demands.
Syrian president Bashar al-Assad sacks his cabinet and suggests significant reforms in his first public intervention in a 10-day-old nationwide uprising.
Bashar al-Assad is preparing to deliver a televised address to the nation amid unprecedented protests, with expectations that he will announce reforms including the repeal of emergency law.

President Bashar al-Assad has begun announcing a series of reforms, including a decree granting citizenship to some stateless Kurds and lifting the ban on teachers wearing the niqab, aimed at placating Sunni Muslims and the Kurdish minority amid growing protests.
Bashar al-Assad promised to end Syria's 48-year emergency law and implement further reforms, but protesters rejected the move as too little, too late.
Syrian security forces opened fire on thousands of protesters gathered in Clock Square in Homs, as part of the ongoing uprising against President Bashar al-Assad's regime.

The Syrian government abrogates its emergency law, described as Bashar al-Assad's biggest concession yet to the protest movement, a day after demonstrations in Homs were violently crushed by security forces.
Security forces loyal to President Bashar al-Assad reportedly opened fire on protesters across dozens of Syrian towns and cities, killing at least 88 people on the bloodiest day of the uprising.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad faces public condemnation from Britain and calls for punitive sanctions from Human Rights Watch after reports of shootings and mass arrests of opposition supporters, with activists saying 120 people died in weekend violence.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad insisted his regime was immune to popular unrest, citing Syria's clear ideology, continuing resistance to Israel, and popular support for the government, as recalled by UK Foreign Secretary William Hague in parliament.
Bashar al-Assad is reported to be intensifying a security-led crackdown on unrest in Syria, with no sign of softening his stance despite international pressure.
The Assad regime deployed armed security forces across more than 50 locations in a violent crackdown on a "day of rage" protests, with over 400 lives claimed in recent weeks.
Protests against President Bashar al-Assad and his regime continue into their third month, with opposition figures emerging as possible leaders.
The Syrian government said it would open a national dialogue amid ongoing anti-government protests against President Bashar al-Assad's regime.
France's foreign minister, Alain Juppé, said that Bashar al-Assad had lost his legitimacy to rule.

Syrian forces reportedly massed tanks outside Jisr al-Shughour as the regime of President Bashar al-Assad began a new military operation there, amid reports of troop defections and a crackdown on the uprising.

US defence secretary Robert Gates suggests President Bashar al-Assad has lost the legitimacy to rule Syria amid reports of army divisions and defections during the crackdown on the pro-democracy uprising.

Syrian troops continued a military assault on Jisr al-Shughour as part of the regime’s effort to crush a sustained challenge to President Bashar al-Assad, causing more than 5,000 refugees to flee into Turkey.

Bashar al-Assad gave a speech offering multi-party elections and a diminished role for the Ba'ath party, but protests erupted across Syria afterward and the speech failed to meet opposition demands for an immediate timetable for radical reform and an end to the army's crackdown.
Syrians hold mass anti-regime protests dismissing President Bashar al-Assad's reform offers as too little and too late, with at least eight people killed.

Syrian authorities set a date for a "national dialogue" with government opponents beginning on 10 July, after President Bashar al-Assad met two visiting westerners, as activists dismissed the prospect while a crackdown continued.
Syrians begin to imagine a future without Assad rule as protests and regime violence polarize Damascus, with over 1,500 civilians killed since mid-March.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad sacks the governor of Hama after 200,000 people protested against his regime.
Syrian state media escalates propaganda exalting Bashar al-Assad amid a bloody crackdown on protests that has killed at least 1,500 people.

Hundreds of thousands of Syrians protest across the country calling for the overthrow of the regime and the departure of President Bashar al-Assad, with at least 11 people reported killed by security forces.

Syria's cabinet backed a draft law to allow rival political parties to President Bashar al-Assad's ruling Ba'ath party for the first time in decades, though opposition groups largely dismissed the move as an empty gesture.
Syrian troops and tanks launched a nationwide assault, including on Hama, killing dozens of protesters against President Bashar al-Assad's regime.
Bashar al-Assad announced an end to one-party rule in Syria while his security forces continued killing protesters.

Syrian opposition activists appeal to the international community to increase pressure on Bashar al-Assad's regime, as condemnation mounts over escalating bloodshed and more than 100 people were reportedly killed across Syria on Sunday.

An opinion article argues that Bashar al-Assad's regime has lost all legitimacy amid a five-month-old Syrian uprising and calls for the international community to reject the regime's claim that it is defending the country from sectarian divisions.

Tens of thousands of Syrians protest against President Bashar al-Assad's regime and in support of Hama residents, as troops open fire on demonstrators after Friday prayers, killing at least 13 people amid a government assault on Hama.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad rejected a Turkish appeal to change tack or meet the fate of Libya's Muammar Gaddafi, as security forces launched another wave of violence against pro-democracy protesters.
Syrian activists fear a government crackdown during Ramadan could stall the uprising against Bashar al-Assad's regime, as the port city of Latakia remains under siege with more raids and arrests.
Bashar al-Assad gave a defiant live televised address warning against outside interference and repeating promises of reform amid a continuing crackdown on protests.

An opinion article argues that the fall of Bashar al-Assad's regime is inevitable as the uprising widens and key constituencies withdraw support, while noting no call for external military intervention inside Syria.

Syrian protesters called for international intervention, including a no-fly zone or protection force, against Bashar al-Assad's regime, with at least two protesters killed as security forces fired on demonstrators.
Russia rebuffs Western attempts to increase pressure on Bashar al-Assad's regime, with President Dmitry Medvedev saying additional pressure is "absolutely not needed."
Turkey imposes sanctions on Bashar al-Assad's regime in protest over its military crackdown.

Bashar al-Assad gave an interview to the Telegraph on the eve of a particularly bloody weekend, during which his security forces killed more than 40 people in a few days and Homs was under a sustained assault.
Syria accepted an Arab League initiative to halt violence, free prisoners, and open dialogue with the opposition, amid skepticism from opponents of President Bashar al-Assad and Western governments.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's government said it would implement in full an Arab League plan to end seven months of violence, though no timetable was laid down for key steps and up to 20 people were killed nationwide that day.
Jordan's King Abdullah becomes the first Arab leader to call for Syria's president Bashar al-Assad to step down.
Syria calls for an emergency Arab League meeting before its scheduled suspension from the body takes effect on 16 November, following a crackdown on demonstrators and attacks on foreign embassies.
Jordan's King Abdullah calls for Bashar al-Assad to step down, underlining the Syrian president's growing regional isolation after Syria's suspension from the Arab League.
The Arab League gave President Bashar al-Assad another 24 hours to accept observers to monitor the violence or face economic sanctions.
The Arab League gives Bashar al-Assad's regime 24 hours to sign an initiative allowing international observers into Syria or face sanctions.
In an interview with ABC's Barbara Walters, Bashar al-Assad denied responsibility for attacks on his own people, saying the forces are not his but belong to the government.

Bashar al-Assad gave an interview with ABC News in which he deflected blame for the brutal repression of his fellow countrymen, saying "I am not in charge of the army" and that he did not feel guilty.
Two of Syria's main opposition groups sign an agreement to set up a democracy if continued mass protests succeed in toppling President Bashar al-Assad.
Bashar al-Assad gave a Damascus speech vowing to crush dissent while promising vague reforms, as the nine-month-old Syrian uprising and pressure for his resignation continued.
Bashar al-Assad condemned the Arab League in a speech in Damascus, calling it a betrayal of Syria and Arabism and characterizing the violence in Syria as an international conspiracy.
Arab and Western governments at the UN Security Council are trying to persuade President Bashar al-Assad to step down.
The Arab League suspended its monitoring mission in Syria and criticized President Bashar al-Assad's regime for escalating violence.
A draft UN Security Council resolution calls on Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to step aside or face "further measures" in 15 days, with a vote expected on Thursday.

Russia declares it will oppose a UN Security Council resolution backed by the US and UK that calls on Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to step down, while the US and UK insist the resolution is peaceful and does not authorize military intervention.

Western countries soften demands in a draft UN Security Council resolution that Bashar al-Assad hand over power to his deputy, dropping an explicit demand for him to step down while still supporting the Arab League's "political transition" plan.
Russia and China veto a UN Security Council resolution on Syria, leaving international diplomacy divided and unable to act against Bashar al-Assad's escalating crackdown.
The UN General Assembly approves a resolution backing an Arab League plan that calls on Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to step down and condemns human rights violations by his regime.
A draft constitution put forward by Bashar al-Assad's regime is set for a referendum in Syria.
Assad's forces are crushing the Baba Amr district of Homs, with reports that more than half the district is under their control as they conduct door-to-door searches.
The Free Syrian Army announces its withdrawal from Baba Amr, and within an hour the Syrian government declares it has taken control of the area.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad told UN-Arab League envoy Kofi Annan that no political progress is possible while "terrorist groups" spread chaos, as Syrian troops launched a fresh assault on Idlib city.
UN special representative Kofi Annan left Damascus after two days of talks with Bashar al-Assad that failed to broker a ceasefire or moves towards one.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad called parliamentary elections for May under a new constitution, as his forces continued a crackdown on opponents.

The Guardian reports that a cache of 3,000 emails allegedly belonging to Bashar al-Assad and his wife Asma is genuine, based on verification including family photographs, identity documents, and confirmation from multiple contacts.
Leaked emails purportedly written by Bashar al-Assad and his wife Asma reveal ordinary personal preoccupations, which the article argues make Assad seem more human rather than more monstrous.

Leaked official Syrian documents reveal that President Bashar al-Assad personally signs off on plans by his government's crisis management centre for a security crackdown to prevent protests from spreading to Damascus.

A former tutor of Bashar al-Assad recalls him as a modest and capable medical student at St Mary's Hospital Medical School in the 1980s, and suggests that from Assad's perspective the situation in Syria may seem "kill or be killed."
Asma al-Assad, the British-born wife of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, is set to be added to an EU sanctions list targeting Syria.

Syria's foreign ministry claims the year-old revolt to topple President Bashar al-Assad is over, while the army continues to shell opposition areas and Assad has accepted Kofi Annan's peace plan that does not demand he step down.

Syria claimed to have begun troop withdrawals from Deraa, Idlib and Zabadani, though the opposition and foreign governments responded skeptically, as violence continued despite the looming UN ceasefire deadline.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad demanded written guarantees from armed opposition groups that they would halt all violence before regime forces would be withdrawn from flashpoints, casting doubt on the UN-backed ceasefire plan.

A UN-backed ceasefire in Syria, intended to pressure President Bashar al-Assad toward a peaceful outcome, began but was only partially observed, with the government accused of not withdrawing troops and heavy weapons from cities.
Russia supported a UN Security Council statement condemning the Houla killings, a move that opened the possibility of US-Russian cooperation to ease Bashar al-Assad out of power.

Russia's foreign minister Sergei Lavrov says both Bashar al-Assad's regime and the armed opposition share responsibility for weekend massacres in Houla and Hama that killed more than 100 people, while continuing to supply arms to Assad.
UN-Arab League envoy Kofi Annan meets with Syrian President Bashar al-Assad in Damascus as international pressure mounts over the Houla massacre.
Russia indicates it will no longer stand in the way of Bashar al-Assad's departure if that is what Syrians want, suggesting a weakening of Moscow's backing for Assad.
Russia stated it would not endorse an internationally backed plan for a political transition in Syria that would require President Bashar al-Assad to surrender power.

US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov are set to meet privately in St Petersburg ahead of an international summit in Geneva aimed at negotiating a political transition that would ease Bashar al-Assad from office.
A UN crisis meeting in Geneva agreed terms for a transitional government in Syria but left unresolved whether Bashar al-Assad could be part of it.

High-level defections, including Syria's ambassador to Baghdad Nawaf al-Fares, are shrinking the area Bashar al-Assad's regime can count on and undermining its claim to represent anyone beyond his family and the Alawite elite.
US sources said Bashar al-Assad's forces had started to move part of Syria's chemical weapons stockpile out of storage facilities, while the Syrian government denied that any had been moved.
Intense clashes between opposition fighters and regime forces loyal to Bashar al-Assad flare in Damascus, marking the most significant fighting in the Syrian capital since the uprising began.
Rebels killed three of Bashar al-Assad's top security chiefs, including his brother-in-law Assef Shawkat and defence minister Dawoud Rajha, in a bomb attack in Damascus.
Bashar al-Assad appeared in Damascus to swear in a new defence minister, his first public appearance since a bomb blast killed three senior officials.
Syria's most senior diplomat in Britain, Khaled al-Ayoubi, defected from the Assad regime, which the UK Foreign Office described as another blow to Bashar al-Assad.

The article reports that the battle for Aleppo is ongoing, with Bashar al-Assad's regime holding the west of the city and the Free Syrian Army the east, and that Assad's army remains intact despite defections and the deaths of four senior security figures.

French President François Hollande urges Syria's divided opposition to form a provisional government, saying Paris would give it official recognition, as Syrian fighter plane attacks on eastern suburbs of Damascus killed at least 60 people according to opposition activists.
Bashar al-Assad said in a rare TV interview that there is no immediate prospect of an end to Syria's civil war and that his armed forces need more time to defeat the opposition.
UN-Arab League envoy Lakhdar Brahimi asked Iran to persuade Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to implement a ceasefire later in October, in tandem with a UN appeal to halt weapons flows to both sides.

UN-Arab League envoy Lakhdar Brahimi told the UN Security Council that Syrian President Bashar al-Assad has accepted a ceasefire for the four-day Eid al-Adha holiday, though there was no confirmation from Damascus and the Syrian foreign ministry said the proposal was still being studied.
A four-day ceasefire in Syria, accepted by Bashar al-Assad's government and several opposition commanders but rejected outright by two Islamist groups, went into effect.

Barack Obama warns Syrian President Bashar al-Assad that any use of chemical weapons would be "totally unacceptable" and would result in "consequences," while Syria denies it would use such weapons against its people.
William Hague says he has seen "some evidence" that Bashar al-Assad's regime is preparing to use chemical weapons against Syrian rebels, while the Syrian regime denies any such plans.
Russia publicly acknowledges for the first time that Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's regime is losing control of the country and that an opposition victory cannot be ruled out.
Vladimir Putin signals that Russia is not preoccupied with the fate of Bashar al-Assad's regime, indicating Moscow may accept that Assad's days are numbered, though without an immediate policy shift.

Bashar al-Assad gave a speech in Damascus proposing a national dialogue and constitutional referendum while urging foreign countries to end support for rebels and pledging to continue fighting "terrorist" violence.
Russia begins a partial evacuation of its citizens from Syria amid civil war, a move interpreted as a lack of faith in Bashar al-Assad's regime's ability to safeguard Russian citizens.
A Lebanese newspaper reports that Bashar al-Assad's wife Asma is pregnant with their fourth child, a claim that remains unconfirmed by the Syrian government.

UK Foreign Secretary William Hague labels Bashar al-Assad "delusional" after Assad accused the British government of "shallow and immature rhetoric" and a "tradition of bullying and hegemony" in a Sunday Times interview.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad warned that the Middle East faces destabilization for decades if rebel forces succeed in overthrowing him, in an interview with Turkish television.

Hassan Nasrallah confirmed for the first time that Hezbollah fighters were helping Bashar al-Assad, while Israel carried out two airstrikes in as many days against stores of Iranian missiles purportedly in transit to Hezbollah and Iran said it was ready to train Assad's army.
Russia defended its arms sales to Syria, including reported deliveries of advanced anti-ship missiles to Bashar al-Assad's forces, saying they would not alter the regional balance of forces.
The British government sent a letter to the UN secretary-general alleging three further incidents of chemical weapons use by Syrian government forces under Bashar al-Assad.
Bashar al-Assad said in an interview with Lebanese TV that Russian S-300 anti-aircraft missiles have arrived in Syria, though US officials said they had no evidence the shipment had arrived.
Clashes erupted in Tripoli between gunmen supporting and opposing Bashar al-Assad amid fighting on the Syrian-Lebanese border involving Hezbollah.
Senator John McCain accuses the Obama administration of sitting idly by while Bashar al-Assad gains the upper hand in Syria's civil war.

Bashar al-Assad claimed last week that S-300 air defence missiles from Russia were on their way, though later Russian media reports said the first shipment would not arrive until the middle of next year.
The US concluded it had evidence that Syrian President Bashar al-Assad had used chemical weapons against the opposition, leading President Obama to authorize military aid to Syrian rebels.
UK Prime Minister David Cameron says Britain shares the US assessment that the regime of President Bashar al-Assad has used chemical weapons against rebels in the Syrian conflict.
Syrian rebels launched a mortar attack on a convoy carrying Bashar al-Assad, leaving him unharmed, though Syria's information minister denied any attack took place.

Syrian opposition groups claim that hundreds of people were killed in chemical weapons attacks by Bashar al-Assad's forces on the outskirts of Damascus, an allegation Syrian state TV denies and that the UN Security Council is to address in an emergency meeting.
A sarin gas attack in Ghouta, which the article states was a turning point that favored Bashar al-Assad's regime rather than the opposition.

Russia calls for a UN inquiry into allegations that the Syrian government of Bashar al-Assad carried out a deadly chemical weapons attack near Damascus, while the US says it has not yet seen conclusive proof.

Vladimir Putin rejects US intelligence claims that Bashar al-Assad's regime used chemical weapons in Syria, calling the attack a provocation by those seeking to draw other countries into the conflict.

Bashar al-Assad or his forces may have stopped using chemical warfare against rebels in the Syrian civil war, though they continue conventional bombardment, and Russia says al-Assad has agreed to draw up an inventory of chemical weapons and sign the Chemical Weapons Convention.
Bashar al-Assad challenged the West to provide a single piece of evidence that he used chemical weapons and warned that military intervention in Syria could spark a regional war.

German newspaper Bild am Sonntag reports, citing unidentified high-level national security sources, that President Bashar al-Assad did not personally order the August 21 chemical weapons attack near Damascus and had blocked numerous requests from his military commanders to use chemical weapons.
Charlie Rose announced he had secured an interview with Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, which was set to air on his television show the following Monday.
US Secretary of State John Kerry says Bashar al-Assad has one week to hand over Syria's chemical weapons to avoid a military attack, while stating he does not expect Assad to comply.
Barack Obama welcomed a Russian proposal for Syria to place its chemical weapons under international control, opening a possible political settlement with Bashar al-Assad's regime.
President Obama cited deterring Bashar al-Assad from using chemical weapons again as a rationale for possible US military force against Syria in a televised address.

US Secretary of State John Kerry says a Russian proposal to place Bashar al-Assad's chemical weapons under international control is the "ideal way" to end the impasse, as the Obama administration agrees to explore the plan's viability at the UN.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad said in an interview that Syria will place its chemical weapons under international control because of Russian diplomatic efforts, not US military threats.

Republican senators John McCain and Lindsey Graham criticize the US-Russia deal on Syria's chemical weapons, saying it would give Syrian President Bashar al-Assad time "to delay and deceive" while the civil war continues.

The US and Russia agree in Geneva on a framework requiring Bashar al-Assad to report Syria's chemical weapons stocks within a week, with UN inspectors to verify by November and stockpiles destroyed by mid-2014.

Vladimir Putin expressed doubts about whether Bashar al-Assad would fulfill the US-Russian plan to identify and destroy Syria's chemical weapons stocks, while saying signs suggest the Syrian regime is serious.
Syrian forces loyal to President Bashar al-Assad killed at least 15 people, including a woman and two children, in an overnight attack on the Sunni Muslim village of Sheikh Hadid north-west of Hama.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad vows to surrender chemical weapons.

Paris prosecutors open a preliminary investigation into the French property portfolio of Rifaat al-Assad, an uncle of Bashar al-Assad, after anti-corruption groups allege he illegally acquired assets worth over €160m.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad sent a private message to Pope Francis via a delegation that met with the pontiff's senior diplomatic representatives, outlining the Syrian government's position ahead of next month's Geneva peace conference.
The Syrian government and rebels seeking to overthrow President Bashar al-Assad agreed to hold their first direct face-to-face negotiations in Geneva.

The first direct negotiations between the Syrian government and rebels seeking to overthrow President Bashar al-Assad started and ended after barely half an hour at the United Nations headquarters in Geneva.

Reports suggest a major new clandestine effort is being planned to open up a "southern front" against the regime of Bashar al-Assad, involving renewed funding, weapons, and intelligence support for moderate rebel groups.
French President François Hollande said France has information that Bashar al-Assad's forces used chemical weapons in recent attacks, though he said the claims had not been proved.
Supporters of Bashar al-Assad stage rallies in Sydney, Adelaide, and Melbourne to help expats register their support ahead of Syria's 3 June presidential election.
Syrians in government-controlled areas voted in a presidential election expected to confirm Bashar al-Assad in office for seven more years, a contest condemned and shunned by his opponents.
Bashar al-Assad was confirmed for a third seven-year term as Syria's president with 88.7% of the vote in an election held only in areas under his control.
Syria's deputy foreign minister Faisal Mekdad says Britain's policy of supporting rebels against Bashar al-Assad is "stupid" and that Britain should apologize and work with Assad to combat terrorism.
Bashar al-Assad was sworn in for a third term as Syria's president in Damascus.
Bashar al-Assad's pitch for an anti-Isis pact with the West falls on closed ears, as David Cameron says Assad is "part of the problem, not part of the solution."

Bashar al-Assad gave a BBC interview in which he denied well-documented use of barrel bombs and made no reference to the Geneva process, drawing criticism that he showed cynicism and self-confidence while the Syrian crisis approached its fourth anniversary.
Bashar al-Assad rejected US calls for negotiations, stating that "declarations from outside do not concern us" and that any talk of the Syrian presidency is for the Syrian people.
Islamist groups led by al-Qaida's Nusra Front took control of the Syrian city of Idlib, dealing a serious blow to President Bashar al-Assad's government.
A former London imam known for his staunch criticism of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad was found shot dead in his car in Wembley, prompting a murder investigation.
Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov called for the US to recognize Syrian president Bashar al-Assad as a partner in the fight against Isis.
Syria rejects a British proposal that Bashar al-Assad could lead a transitional government for up to six months before stepping down.
David Cameron arrives at the United Nations hoping to work with other countries on a deal to end Syria's civil war that could allow President Bashar al-Assad to stay in power for an interim period.

Russia’s military buildup in Syria, including planes, ships, armour and marines sent to Latakia in support of Bashar al-Assad’s fight against Islamic State, further complicates an already complex situation, according to UK defence secretary Michael Fallon.
Saudi Arabia's foreign minister Adel Al-Jubeir says there is "no future" for Bashar al-Assad in Syria, stating he must either leave power through a political transition or be removed by force.
Russia launched airstrikes in Syria that targeted groups opposed to Bashar al-Assad, not only Isis, in a move that could escalate the conflict unless it hastens a political transition.
Russia intervened militarily in Syria to shore up Bashar al-Assad’s position after the fall of Idlib and Jisr al-Shughour exposed the Syrian army’s weakness.
US-backed Syrian rebels say they were hit by Russian airstrikes, with a rebel commander who defected from Bashar al-Assad's army reporting that a training camp in Idlib province was struck.

Barack Obama says Russia's failure to distinguish between Islamic State fighters and moderate opposition forces battling Bashar al-Assad is a "recipe for disaster," as evidence emerges that Moscow is targeting anti-regime rebels rather than just Isis.

Ground troops loyal to Bashar al-Assad launched a major offensive in central Syria backed by Russian airstrikes, the first time Assad's forces coordinated with the Russian airforce to seize lost territory from opposition forces.
Bashar al-Assad met Vladimir Putin in Moscow to thank him for Russia’s military support in Syria, in his first foreign visit since 2011.
International talks on the Syrian crisis in Vienna end without agreement on Bashar al-Assad's fate, as Iran and Saudi Arabia remain divided over whether he must step down.

Syrian National Coalition president Khaled Khoja warned that Russia and Iran cannot be trusted in diplomatic efforts to end the Syria crisis because of their military intervention on the side of President Bashar al-Assad.
Syrian opposition leaders reject Russian peace proposals for ending the country's crisis, reiterating that Bashar al-Assad must step down.
US Secretary of State John Kerry said a ceasefire between Bashar al-Assad and rebels could be weeks away, following a Vienna agreement supporting a 1 January deadline for talks.
Russian foreign minister Sergei Lavrov urged an end to calls for Bashar al-Assad to step down, saying it is unacceptable to insist on his departure.

Saudi Arabia is hosting a conference of Syrian opposition groups aimed at unifying them ahead of talks with Bashar al-Assad, though the opposition remains divided over whether Assad must leave power at the start of any transition.
A Kremlin spokesman denies reports that Vladimir Putin sent a senior intelligence official to Damascus to ask Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to step down.

Forces loyal to Bashar al-Assad, backed by intensive Russian airstrikes, took control of most of the countryside immediately north of Aleppo, pushing tens of thousands of Syrians toward the Turkish border.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad vowed to retake the whole country and warned the war could still take a long time, hours before an agreement was reached in Munich on a cessation of hostilities.
Syrian opposition reacts with guarded optimism to a deal to pause hostilities, but says it does not trust Russia to halt its aerial campaign that enabled advances by forces loyal to Bashar al-Assad.

A deadline to secure a cessation of hostilities in Syria passed, further delaying the resumption of UN-brokered peace talks between Syrian president Bashar al-Assad and rebels fighting to overthrow him.
Syrian Foreign Minister Walid al-Muallem says Bashar al-Assad is a "red line" and that peace talks will fail if any party tries to discuss the presidency in a transition government.
Long-awaited Syria peace talks are due to start in Geneva despite Syrian government calls for the future of President Bashar al-Assad to be excluded from the agenda.
Putin declares withdrawal of majority of Russian troops from Syria, informing Assad personally by telephone.
Syrian government delegation head Bashar Ja'afari says the political future of President Bashar al-Assad has been excluded from negotiations to end the Syrian civil war.

Syrian opposition warns that peace talks in Geneva cannot progress unless Vladimir Putin pressures Bashar al-Assad, and that a ceasefire will collapse if reconvened talks do not move quickly to political transition.
Assad told RIA he could foresee agreement on a political settlement for Syria within weeks, while opposing the formation of a transitional governing body with full executive powers.

Bashar al-Assad and his wife Asma voted near the presidential palace in Damascus in parliamentary elections dismissed by the opposition and Western backers as a sham, as Syrian peace talks resumed in Geneva.

Fighting between rebel forces and President Bashar al-Assad's government forces continues in Aleppo, with Friday prayers cancelled across the city for the first time since the war began and a new partial truce not covering Aleppo.
Boris Johnson says Bashar al-Assad cannot remain in power in Syria as he prepares for his first talks as British foreign secretary with US counterpart John Kerry.
President Bashar al-Assad declared the ceasefire in Syria over and his regime blocked or stalled aid convoys, with an airstrike decimating a UN aid convoy in Aleppo countryside.
